hints: Use the number and type of quark constituents to distinguish a meson from a baryon.
walkthrough: A meson consists of one quark and one antiquark.
Both Q and R have exactly this composition.
Therefore they are mesons; meson is the more specific accepted class, while hadron is the wider class containing mesons.

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies Q and R as mesons, or gives the accepted broader class hadrons.

hints: Add the two constituent charges for each meson, remembering that an antiquark has the opposite charge to its corresponding quark.
The strange quark contributes −1/3e to Q, whereas anti-up contributes −2/3e to R; select a second constituent that gives each stated total.
walkthrough: A strange quark has charge −1/3e. To make Q have total charge −1e, the second constituent must have charge −2/3e, so it may be anti-up, anti-charm or anti-top.
An anti-up quark has charge −2/3e. To make R neutral, the second constituent must have charge +2/3e, so it may be up, charm or top.
One valid completion is Q: anti-up and R: up.

ai_rubric.observable: For Q, gives anti-up, anti-charm or anti-top as the second constituent.
For R, gives up, charm or top as the second constituent.
